summary.headline: Paisalo Q1 FY27: record disbursement of Rs.17,309 million (+128% YoY), PAT up 30% to Rs.613 million, gross NPA 0.70%.
summary.overview: Management, represented solely by Deputy MD Santanu Agarwal (CFO unavailable), reported AUM of Rs.67,074 million (+28% YoY) and a record quarterly disbursement of Rs.17,309 million. Total income rose 19% YoY to Rs.2,603 million and PAT rose 30% YoY to Rs.613 million, with gross NPA at 0.70% and net NPA at 0.49%. Management set a three-year ambition to roughly double AUM, income and profitability, and launched a Rs.300 crore NCD tranche under a Rs.900 crore shelf. Sequential metrics were weaker in several places: interest expense rose and opex fell sharply QoQ, and loan-loss provisions jumped, which management attributed to timing and settlement effects.

financial_highlights.change: expected to stay slightly higher short term

segments.name: Lending (MSME / micro-enterprise)
segments.commentary: AUM mix in Q1: food and hospitality about 23%, agri and allied agri about 15%, street vendors about 16%; vehicle, health, education and textile each about 3-6%. Internal cap is 25% per industry.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Touch points rose to 5,995 across 23 states from 5,299 a quarter earlier (+696 over four quarters per management). BC franchise crossed USD 1 billion gross transaction value.

segments.name: New product lines
segments.commentary: Six new product lines added in the last quarter across mobility, industrial, medical, agri equipment and alternative fuel; too early to set mix targets.

guidance_outlook: Ambition to approximately double AUM, income and profitability over three fiscal years.
Quarterly growth may normalise from the high base, but management expects healthy momentum through FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio to stay slightly higher in the short to medium term during the AI transition.
Co-lending with SBI remains at status quo, awaiting compliance on the bank side; treated as optionality not included in guidance.
Three new development products to launch around end-Q3 FY27; AI outbound calling for new-to-Paisalo customers to start around then.
Internal leverage comfort around 3.5x against a regulatory limit of 7x; about $44 million of FCCBs pending conversion, with a committee meeting scheduled.
risks_watch: Interest cost (Rs.115 crore per the questioner's reading, up from Rs.87 crore QoQ) and sharp opex fall (Rs.69 crore to Rs.46 crore) partly unexplained; management cites timing lag between funding and deployment.
Loan-loss provisions up sharply QoQ (about 120% per the questioner); management attributes this to settlement timing.
Collection efficiency 97.5%, reportedly down about 1% QoQ.
Leverage (debt-to-equity 2.61x) rising; headroom depends on FCCB conversion and the NCD issue.
Co-lending with SBI stalled pending bank compliance; RBI co-lending and collateral-free rule changes need to be operationalised.
New product lines (six added recently) have short track records; risks not yet quantified.
Management declined to disclose new-to-Paisalo AI outbound conversion metrics until around end-Q3 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, distribution and AI; repeated the 'strongest quarter yet' framing. Evasive or deflecting on sequential cost, interest and provision questions, which were answered with timing explanations and without quantified guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SBI co-lending tie-up that was expected to expand in Q1 and Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Status quo, same as last quarter; awaiting compliance on the bank side before work can start, so disbursements have been slow.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran war and commodity prices on borrowers and NPLs?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact limited, as most borrowers are micro-enterprises and traders; large manufacturers and exporters affected. Loan-loss provisions rose sequentially but remain well below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income trend and how much more efficiency can AI unlock?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income is about 40% and expected to stay slightly higher in the short-to-medium term during the AI transition; normalisation is a longer-term expectation with no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Interest expense rose from Rs.87 crore to Rs.115 crore QoQ while opex fell from Rs.69 crore to Rs.46 crore, and provisions rose about 120% QoQ. Why?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to timing lag between debt raising and deployment into loans; Q2 NCD and possible FCCB conversion expected to normalise cost. Credit costs below 2% ex-COVID and below 1% over five years; YoY loan losses down about 10%; Q1 provisions reflect short-term provisioning to speed settlements. Pledges down QoQ; promoters acquired 4.7% in open market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target AUM mix for agri, industrial and alternative fuel equipment, and the risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No target mix given; the six new products are being given equal weight, so agri could move from about 15% to 20% or lower, and vehicle could rise from 3% to 10%; no product to exceed 25% of AUM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the internal leverage ceiling and remaining borrowing headroom given debt-to-equity rising to 2.61x?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal comfort around 3.5x against the regulatory limit of 7x; debt-to-equity was about 2.4-2.5x excluding the FCCBs, and about $44 million of FCCBs pending conversion with a committee meeting scheduled.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale behind promoter stake increases and is it a valuation signal?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters have acquired 4.7% from the open market, largely exhausting the 5% annual limit; promoters also invested about Rs.180-185 crore via warrants three to four years ago. Management framed it as conviction in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key drivers and timeline for the doubling of AUM, income and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Four pillars: distribution, product diversification, AI and liability management. Target is three fiscal years; co-lending with SBI is optionality not included in the target.

capex_capacity: Touch points rose to 5,995 across 23 states at end-Q1 FY27 from 5,299 a quarter earlier; management cited about 696 additions over the last four quarters.
Business correspondent franchise crossed USD 1 billion in gross transaction value during the quarter.

AI scale-up: about 1,80,000 customer on-boarding applications in Q1 vs about 1,60,000 in Q4 FY26; about 5,00,000 voice-to-data conversions vs 3,50,000; AI outbound calls about 2,00,000 per day vs about 1,50,000; AI bots increased from 7 to 18.
Revamped branch and BC application platform (AI-assisted digital journey) in advanced stages; rollout framed as a next-leg catalyst, no date given.

Three new development products to launch around end-Q3 FY27; AI outbound calling for new-to-Paisalo customers to begin around then. Asset-light expansion via institutional and OEM partnerships; no capex figures disclosed.
demand_pricing: Record Q1 FY27 disbursement of Rs.17,309 million, +128% YoY, attributed to deeper penetration via increased touch points and strong MSME/SME demand.
Management expects quarterly growth to normalise from the high base but healthy momentum through FY27.
AUM mix in Q1: food and hospitality about 23%, agri and allied agri about 15%, street vendors about 16%; vehicle, health, education and textile about 3-6% each; internal cap 25% per industry.
Six new product lines added in the last quarter (mobility, industrial, medical, agri equipment, alternative fuel); management said mix targets are too early to set.
Cost of borrowing 10.1%, down 64 bps YoY and about 300 bps below the 13% of FY21.
RBI circular raising collateral-free lending threshold for MSMEs to Rs.20 lakh; about 93% of Paisalo's portfolio is secured and about 7% unsecured per management.
key_quotes: Paisalo has delivered one of its strongest quarters yet across growth, distribution, technology and asset quality and we believe the momentum we are seeing is not just continuing but building.
During Q1 FY2027, we disbursed Rs.17,309 million, an exceptional 128% year-on-year growth.

So typically what happens is that towards the end of the Q4 level, most of the borrowers and most of the segments that are going into the loan loss segment are willing to come and sit on the table for settlement and we are also doing that settlement faster because we have Q4 end.
we are targeting three fiscal years for achieving our target of doubling of our AUM income and PAT.
